domains.label: Atmosphere
domains.description: Meteorological forcing, surface energy exchange, and steam microclimate.

domains.label: Cryosphere & soil
domains.description: Snow accumulation and melt, soil storage, and evapotranspiration.

domains.label: Geosphere
domains.description: Geothermal heat, thermal pools, ground temperature, and hot-water outflow processes.

domains.label: Hydrosphere
domains.description: Water and heat transport along the mapped Firehole channel, with prescribed inflows.

domains.label: Terrestrial biosphere
domains.description: Vegetation stocks, canopy structure, grazing, and mammal guild responses.

domains.label: Aquatic biosphere
domains.description: Temperature, oxygen, food resources, and habitat suitability in the river.

nodes.label: Reach mixing
nodes.equations: rho*cp*d(V_i*T_i)/dt = rho*cp*(Q_in*T_in - Q_out*T_i) + rho*cp*sum(Q_l*T_l - Q_l*T_i) + A_i*h_i*(T_air - T_i); Q_out = Q_in + sum(Q_l)
nodes.assumptions: each reach fully mixed; volumes fixed; lateral sources prescribed; rho and cp constant
nodes.limits: uniform-flow resistance; backwater, jumps, floodplain exchange excluded
nodes.units: time s; temperature C; discharge m3/s; volume m3; coefficient W/m2/K; area m2
nodes.variables: V_i: reach volume m3; T_i: reach temperature C; Q_in, Q_out, Q_l: discharges m3/s; T_in, T_l: upstream and lateral temperatures C; A_i: reach surface area m2; h_i: Newton coefficient W/m2/K; T_air: air temperature C
nodes.model_level: quasi-steady reach network with constant volumes
nodes.summary: River temperatures are reported for six reaches. The data view uses flow-weighted channel temperatures.

nodes.label: Heat transport
nodes.equations: rho*cp*V_i*dT_i/dt = rho*cp*(F_in,i - F_out,i) + rho*cp*sum(Q_l*T_l) + A_surface,i*Phi_surface,i + P_cell,i; F_j = Q_j*T_upwind + G_j*(T_left - T_right); G_j = harmonic dispersion conductance; backward Euler, tridiagonal solve
nodes.assumptions: prescribed upstream Q/T series; DEM-derived depths; authored roughness; rho and cp constant
nodes.limits: depths estimated from DEM transects; submerged bathymetry unmeasured
nodes.units: time s; temperature C; discharge m3/s; conductance m3/s; flux W/m2; power W; area m2; volume m3
nodes.variables: V_i: cell water volume m3; Q_j: face discharge m3/s; G_j: face dispersive conductance m3/s; Phi_surface: surface heat flux W/m2; P_cell: cell heat power W; A_surface,i: cell surface area m2
nodes.model_level: 1-D advection-dispersion on chainage cells, no momentum equation
nodes.summary: River flow carries heat downstream. Mixing, lateral inflows, and exchange with the surroundings change water temperature.

nodes.label: Surface heat exchange
nodes.equations: Newton: Phi = h(Tair - T); explicit: Phi = SW + LW + H + LE with scaled turbulent coefficients c_h, c_e; nonlinear closure solved by damped Newton iteration
nodes.assumptions: explicit-budget coefficients illustrative; ice-free surface
nodes.limits: winter ice cover outside scope; radiation and transfer coefficients require local calibration; convergence is numerical, not validation
nodes.units: temperature C; flux W/m2; coefficient W/m2/K
nodes.variables: Phi: surface heat flux W/m2; T, Tair: surface and air temperatures C; h: Newton coefficient W/m2/K; SW, LW, H, LE: shortwave, longwave, sensible, latent fluxes W/m2
nodes.model_level: lumped Newton exchange by default; explicit nonlinear surface budget solved by damped Newton iteration
nodes.summary: The river gains or loses heat across its surface. The selected exchange model determines which effects are calculated separately.

nodes.label: Thermal plume
nodes.equations: u dT/dz = Dx d2T/dx2 + Dz d2T/dz2 - k(T - ambient); implicit upwind/centered solve, source cells fixed
nodes.assumptions: map overlay for field notes; velocity and diffusivities prescribed
nodes.limits: no calibration; cross-channel mixing unresolved
nodes.units: velocity m/s; diffusivity m2/s; rate 1/s; temperature C
nodes.variables: u: streamwise velocity m/s; Dx, Dz: diffusivities m2/s; k: relaxation to ambient 1/s; T, ambient: temperatures C
nodes.model_level: steady 2-D advection-diffusion solve on a fixed grid
nodes.summary: A steady temperature field represents the spread of heat away from a thermal source.

nodes.label: Pool temperature
nodes.equations: T(r) = T_edge + (T_center - T_edge)*(1-(r/r_water)^2) for 0 <= r <= r_water; T = T_edge for r > r_water; pigment bands authored
nodes.assumptions: T_center is a published point sample where one exists; T_edge, pigment stops, and depths other than a published lower bound are authored; outline traced from lidar where adopted
nodes.limits: no radial temperature measurement; no universal temperature-to-color relation; bathymetry unmeasured
nodes.units: radius m; temperature C
nodes.variables: r: radial coordinate m; r_water: water edge radius m; T_center, T_edge: center and edge temperatures C
nodes.model_level: diagnostic radial profile, no heat PDE
nodes.summary: Pool outlines come from airborne lidar or a mapped polygon. Center temperatures are published point samples where labeled; edge temperatures, radial profiles, depths, and color bands are authored.

nodes.label: Vegetation
nodes.equations: dB/dt = r f_light f_water B(1 - B/K) - G
nodes.assumptions: patch-mean moisture and light; suitability coefficients authored
nodes.limits: no organism counts; K and r uncalibrated
nodes.units: biomass kg/m2; capacity kg/m2; rate 1/s; grazing kg/m2/s
nodes.variables: B: biomass kg/m2; K: carrying capacity kg/m2; r: intrinsic growth rate 1/s; f_light, f_water: modifiers dimensionless; G: grazing debit kg/m2/s
nodes.model_level: lumped logistic growth with grazing debit per patch
nodes.summary: Vegetation biomass changes with modeled growth and grazing.

nodes.label: Insect life stages
nodes.equations: C(N) = aN/(1 + ahN); benthic degree-day development to emergence flux
nodes.assumptions: hourly substeps; shared foraging ground at refuge cell
nodes.limits: molluscs unmodeled; warm-cell food underestimated
nodes.units: density dimensionless; time s; temperature C
nodes.variables: N: prey density dimensionless; a: attack rate; h: handling time; degree_days: accumulated TAVG above base C*day
nodes.model_level: three-compartment prey with Holling-II depletion
nodes.summary: The compartment model tracks aquatic and terrestrial insect stocks and consumption.

nodes.label: Trout habitat
nodes.equations: Ui = wf Fi + wc Ci - wt phi(Ti) - wv Vi - wd Di; refuge by argmax in swim range
nodes.assumptions: literature anchors for thermal terms; weights authored; uniform depth 1.1 m
nodes.limits: shelter positioning, no mortality; sub-cell refuges unresolved
nodes.units: temperature C; depth m; velocity m/s; weights dimensionless
nodes.variables: Fi, Ci, Ti, Vi, Di: food, cover, temperature penalty, velocity, depth terms; w_*: authored weights; U_i: nondimensional suitability
nodes.model_level: nondimensional suitability over chainage window
nodes.summary: Trout habitat suitability combines water temperature, food, cover, depth, and flow conditions.

nodes.label: Grazing routes
nodes.equations: Euclidean-heuristic shortest path with full-segment blocked checks
nodes.assumptions: thermal, water, cliff exclusion masks; sparse authored loops
nodes.limits: no abundance model; corridor re-walk covers the authored route
nodes.units: length m; grid spacing m
nodes.variables: waypoints: (x, z) m; cell_m: grid spacing m; eligibility: boolean mask
nodes.model_level: 8-connected A* on eligibility grid, no movement dynamics
nodes.summary: Authored paths place grazing animals in the scene. They are not observed movement tracks.

nodes.label: Solute transport
nodes.equations: V_i dC_i/dt = Q_j C_upwind - Q_{j+1} C_i + G_j (C_left - C_right) + sum(Q_l C_l)
nodes.assumptions: chloride and boron conservative; arsenic conservative in scope
nodes.limits: no photochemistry, no pH-driven sorption cycling
nodes.units: concentration mg/L or ug/L; discharge m3/s
nodes.variables: C_i: cell concentration mg/L or ug/L; Q: face discharge m3/s; G: dispersive conductance m3/s; Q_l C_l: lateral source mass flux
nodes.model_level: 1-D advection-dispersion on chainage cells, backward Euler, three conservative solutes
nodes.summary: The river transports dissolved chloride, arsenic, and boron with flowing and mixing water.

nodes.label: Dissolved oxygen
nodes.equations: V_i dC_i/dt = Q (C_up - C_i) + V_i k2 (C_sat - C_i) + V_i (GPP - R); C_sat Benson Krause 1984
nodes.assumptions: ice free surface; Covar regime selects formula
nodes.limits: no sediment oxygen demand; no reactive transport
nodes.units: concentration mg/L; rate 1/day; metabolism mg/L/s
nodes.variables: C_i: DO mg/L; k2: reaeration 1/day; GPP, R: periphyton metabolism mg O2 per L per s
nodes.model_level: implicit upwind reach with Covar reaeration regime
nodes.summary: Dissolved oxygen responds to transport, exchange with air, and biological production and respiration.

nodes.label: Periphyton
nodes.equations: dB/dt = (P_max tanh(I/Ik) f_T(T) f_shade(B) - R(T, B) - G(B, grazer)) B
nodes.assumptions: photosynthetic quotient 1.2; Eppley slope 0.0633 per C
nodes.limits: no nutrient dynamics beyond authored factor; no sloughing event
nodes.units: biomass mg C/m2; light W/m2; rates 1/day
nodes.variables: B: biomass mg C/m2; P_max: specific GPP 1/day; Ik: saturation light W/m2; I: PAR W/m2
nodes.model_level: logistic biomass with Platt-Jassby light response and Eppley temperature factor
nodes.summary: Attached algae grow with light and temperature and contribute to the river's oxygen balance.

nodes.label: Canopy & terrain shade
nodes.equations: shortwave_multiplier = 0.8 direct_beam_fraction + 0.2 sky_view_factor
nodes.assumptions: 0.8 direct 0.2 diffuse clear-sky midday split (Reindl 1990)
nodes.limits: aerosol and multiple scattering absent
nodes.units: dimensionless multipliers
nodes.variables: sky view factor: hemispherical integral of blocked sky; direct beam fraction: canopy transmissivity along sun bearing
nodes.model_level: DEM horizon sampling with canopy direct beam blocking
nodes.summary: Terrain and canopy reduce the sunlight available to the river.

nodes.label: Ground heat
nodes.equations: T(z) = T_surface + Q z / k capped at local boiling point; melt_mm_d = Q / (rho_water L_f) in mm/day
nodes.assumptions: steady state; boiling cap at FAO-56 Eq 7 pressure
nodes.limits: no transient heat storage; no fumarole venting
nodes.units: flux W/m2; conductivity W/m/K; depth m; melt mm/day
nodes.variables: Q: ground heat flux W/m2; k: sinter conductivity W/m/K; z: depth m; L_f: latent heat of fusion J/kg
nodes.model_level: mask-selected heat flux with steady conductive profile
nodes.summary: Prescribed geothermal heat flux warms the ground and contributes energy to snowmelt.

nodes.label: Reference ET
nodes.equations: ET0 = (0.408 Delta (Rn - G) + gamma 900/(T+273) u2 (es - ea)) / (Delta + gamma (1 + 0.34 u2))
nodes.assumptions: short grass reference; Kc authored per patch type
nodes.limits: no stress formulation beyond relative soil water scaling
nodes.units: ET0 mm/day; temperature C; radiation MJ/m2/day; wind m/s
nodes.variables: Delta: slope svp kPa/C; gamma: psychrometric kPa/C; Rn: net radiation MJ/m2/day; es, ea: svp and vapor pressure kPa; u2: wind at 2 m m/s
nodes.model_level: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference and Kc crop coefficients
nodes.summary: Reference evapotranspiration estimates atmospheric water demand. The soil-water model owns the actual water loss.

nodes.label: Piscivores
nodes.equations: mortality = sum_i density_i intake_i(N) share_i exp(-depth / depth_scale_i) / N
nodes.assumptions: authored illustrative densities; exponential depth refuge
nodes.limits: no spatial pursuit; no diel visitation
nodes.units: mortality 1/day; density 1/m; depth m
nodes.variables: density: per m river; intake: per capita per day; share: size class fraction; depth_scale: m
nodes.model_level: per predator Holling II with depth refuge factor
nodes.summary: An authored predator population applies a depth-dependent predation pressure to modeled trout habitat.

nodes.label: Aerial insectivores
nodes.equations: C(N) = aN/(1 + ahN) with per-consumer attack and handling
nodes.assumptions: swallow bat and riparian spider diet shares authored
nodes.limits: no breeding phenology; no colony-size dynamics
nodes.units: density dimensionless; time days
nodes.variables: N: emergent prey density; a: attack rate; h: handling time per capita
nodes.model_level: Holling II offtake on emergent prey compartment
nodes.summary: Emerging insects feed modeled predators along the river.

nodes.label: Outflow food web
nodes.equations: dN/dt = r_max N (1 - N/K) - m(flow_cv) N - sum predators Holling II; K from fly window and mat
nodes.assumptions: Paracoenia and Ephydra windows below 40 C
nodes.limits: no spatial propagation; no sediment feedback
nodes.units: density 1/m2; rate 1/day
nodes.variables: N: fly density per m2; m: mite parasitism rate 1/day; flow_cv: outflow discharge CV; K: carrying density
nodes.model_level: logistic brine fly recruitment with mite parasitism and Holling II predators
nodes.summary: Thermal outflow temperature and microbial mats influence the modeled food resources available to flies and their consumers.

nodes.label: Steam microclimate
nodes.equations: Phi_s = rho c_h |U| (T_s - T_a); Phi_e = rho L c_e |U| (q_s - q_a); h_i = A z0 (fetch/z0)^B
nodes.assumptions: ice-free; flat terrain; shared surface flux defaults
nodes.limits: no three dimensional advection; no convective plume
nodes.units: flux W/m2; temperature C; humidity dimensionless; fetch m; roughness m
nodes.variables: Phi_s, Phi_e: sensible and latent fluxes W/m2; h_i: internal boundary layer m; A, B: authored power-law coefficients
nodes.model_level: bulk aerodynamic plume with internal boundary layer
nodes.summary: A saved plume calculation estimates how hot-water sources warm and humidify downwind air.

nodes.label: Benthic food web
nodes.equations: B_new = B exp(-decay dt) + emergence(T, dd); survival = ramp(DO, lethal, sensitive); grazer competition = 1 + weight mudsnail density
nodes.assumptions: Davis 1975 DO anchors; Mackey 1977 chironomid envelope
nodes.limits: no life stage structure; no drift
nodes.units: biomass dimensionless; time days; DO mg/L
nodes.variables: B: taxon biomass; dd: degree days above tbase; DO: oxygen mg/L; mudsnail density: competitor state
nodes.model_level: per taxon degree day emergence with DO survival ramp
nodes.summary: Benthic invertebrates respond to temperature, oxygen, development, and competition.

nodes.label: Snow & soil storage
nodes.equations: SWE_{t+1} = max(0, SWE_t + P_t - M_t); M_t = k_melt*max(0, TAVG_t - T_base) + ground_energy_mm_d; soil_{t+1} = clip(soil_t + infiltration - ET - drainage)
nodes.assumptions: daily TAVG forcing; precipitation is liquid-equivalent daily accumulation; habitat modifiers authored; thermal ground carries melt flux
nodes.limits: TAVG forcing misses plateau melt energy; soil moisture unvalidated
nodes.units: SWE mm; precipitation mm/day; melt mm/day; temperature C; soil mm
nodes.variables: SWE: snow water equivalent mm; P: precipitation liquid-equivalent daily accumulation mm/day; M: daily melt mm/day; k_melt: mm/C/day; TAVG: daily mean air temperature C; T_base: 0 C; ground_energy_mm_d: mm/day; soil: soil water mm
nodes.model_level: degree-day accumulation/melt with soil bucket
nodes.summary: The snow and soil model tracks stored water and water loss within each patch.

nodes.label: Mammal guilds
nodes.equations: activity = food*water_access*thermal_response*snow_access*season*diel; birth = N*(1-N)*(1-exp(-birth_rate*activity*dt/year)); mortality and predation remove bounded fractions using exponential hazards; forage_consumed = min(available_stock, authored_demand)
nodes.assumptions: primary park occurrence records constrain roster; habitat traits, local populations, resource conversion, hazards and display encounter probabilities are authored
nodes.limits: no field-fitted local abundance, mortality, energy transfer or sighting frequencies; observation encounters are separate from ecological populations; unconfirmed and unsuitable local taxa are gated
nodes.units: time s; hazard 1/year; population and vegetation relative indices
nodes.variables: N: authored population equivalent per species and patch; activity: relative index; dt: physical elapsed seconds; rates: authored per-year hazards; forage: normalized vegetation biomass index
nodes.model_level: bounded authored population equivalents with habitat, resource, weather and predator-prey response
nodes.summary: Authored mammal population indices respond to habitat, forage, water access, weather, and season.

nodes.label: Upstream boundary
nodes.model_level: Prescribed upstream discharge and temperature.
nodes.assumptions: Upstream forcing is specified by the scenario.
nodes.limits: Discharge and upstream temperature are prescribed inputs.
nodes.units: m3/s; C
nodes.summary: Upstream flow and temperature are supplied to the model as scenario inputs.

nodes.label: Lateral inflows
nodes.model_level: Water and heat enter at specified connection locations.
nodes.assumptions: Source temperatures and discharges are authored.
nodes.limits: Local source hydrographs are unmeasured.
nodes.units: m3/s; C
nodes.summary: Lateral inflows add water and heat at specified locations along the river.

nodes.label: Downstream export
nodes.model_level: Water and thermal energy leave the modeled channel.
nodes.assumptions: Advective outflow; zero dispersive boundary flux.
nodes.limits: The downstream river is outside the modeled reach.
nodes.units: m3/s; J/s
nodes.summary: The modeled river exports water and heat through its downstream boundary.

nodes.label: Weather forcing
nodes.summary: Scenario weather supplies atmospheric forcing. Temperature follows an authored daily cycle; the remaining variables use the saved scenario inputs.
nodes.model_level: Authored meteorological forcing with a shared simulation epoch and computed solar geometry.
nodes.assumptions: Air temperature follows an authored daily cycle. Wind, humidity, and cloud are scenario inputs.
nodes.limits: The selected weather is not a record of observed conditions.
nodes.units: C; m/s; relative humidity; solar angles in degrees

nodes.label: Microbial mats
nodes.summary: The model assigns microbial communities and pigments to thermal surfaces.
nodes.model_level: Spatial community and biomass representation with temperature and substrate gates.
nodes.assumptions: Community response and pigment appearance combine literature relationships with authored values.
nodes.limits: Local biomass and color have no completed field evaluation. Color alone does not determine water temperature.
nodes.units: Community classes; model biomass and appearance fields

nodes.label: Outflow cooling
nodes.summary: Hot water cools along mapped outflow paths as its surface exchanges energy with the surroundings.
nodes.model_level: Steady energy balance over a routed thin water film.
nodes.assumptions: Spring temperatures, discharges, and minimum film depth are authored.
nodes.limits: Film depths and local outflow temperatures are unmeasured.
nodes.units: Temperature C; flow m3/s; heat flux W/m2

nodes.label: Canopy structure
nodes.summary: LiDAR data locate dominant crowns and estimate their height and conservative crown-core area.
nodes.model_level: Derived crown census and canopy coverage estimates from frozen point-cloud inputs.
nodes.assumptions: Segmentation and donor-tree relationships introduce authored and transferred values.
nodes.limits: Detected crowns are not a census of all stems. Species and local detection error are not established.
nodes.units: Crown dimensions m; canopy fraction

nodes.label: Channel-bed heat exchange
nodes.summary: Heat moves between river water and a represented subsurface water store according to their temperature difference.
nodes.model_level: Analytic exchange between coupled channel and storage-zone heat reservoirs.
nodes.assumptions: Storage volumes and exchange rates are authored.
nodes.limits: Local hyporheic flow paths and exchange rates are unmeasured.
nodes.units: Stored heat J; temperature C

nodes.label: Dynamic flow routing
nodes.summary: A momentum-based river model would represent changing discharge and water levels. The selected model prescribes inflow and uses fixed channel volumes.
nodes.model_level: A momentum-based river model would represent changing discharge and water levels. The selected model prescribes inflow and uses fixed channel volumes.
nodes.assumptions: Absent from the selected model formulation.
nodes.limits: No results for this extension are represented in this snapshot.
nodes.units: Not applicable

nodes.label: Winter ice cover
nodes.summary: An ice-cover energy balance would extend river heat exchange into frozen conditions. The selected surface formulation is ice-free.
nodes.model_level: An ice-cover energy balance would extend river heat exchange into frozen conditions. The selected surface formulation is ice-free.
nodes.assumptions: Absent from the selected model formulation.
nodes.limits: No results for this extension are represented in this snapshot.
nodes.units: Not applicable

nodes.label: Reactive chemistry
nodes.summary: Chemical reactions could change dissolved constituents during transport. The current model treats them as conservative.
nodes.model_level: Chemical reactions could change dissolved constituents during transport. The current model treats them as conservative.
nodes.assumptions: Absent from the selected model formulation.
nodes.limits: No results for this extension are represented in this snapshot.
nodes.units: Not applicable

nodes.label: Snow-data assimilation
nodes.summary: Assimilating spatial snow observations could constrain snow storage. The selected scenario uses authored forcing and a snow-soil model.
nodes.model_level: Assimilating spatial snow observations could constrain snow storage. The selected scenario uses authored forcing and a snow-soil model.
nodes.assumptions: Absent from the selected model formulation.
nodes.limits: No results for this extension are represented in this snapshot.
nodes.units: Not applicable

nodes.label: Canopy interception
nodes.summary: A canopy water store could track rain before it evaporates or reaches the ground. That store is absent from the current model.
nodes.model_level: A canopy water store could track rain before it evaporates or reaches the ground. That store is absent from the current model.
nodes.assumptions: Absent from the selected model formulation.
nodes.limits: No results for this extension are represented in this snapshot.
nodes.units: Not applicable

nodes.label: Surveyed channel depths
nodes.summary: Submerged channel surveys could replace authored depth estimates and constrain velocity and thermal residence time.
nodes.model_level: Submerged channel surveys could replace authored depth estimates and constrain velocity and thermal residence time.
nodes.assumptions: Absent from the selected model formulation.
nodes.limits: No results for this extension are represented in this snapshot.
nodes.units: Not applicable

edges.label: upstream water inflow
edges.method: advective face flux with zero dispersive boundary flux
edges.summary: Water enters the river at a prescribed flow rate. The scenario supplies this upstream discharge.

edges.label: thermal energy carried by upstream inflow
edges.method: face discharge times boundary temperature
edges.summary: Incoming water carries heat. Its temperature and flow set the upstream thermal input.

edges.label: tributary water inflow per source
edges.method: one solver Source per ecosystem lateral
edges.summary: Tributaries and thermal outflows add water at specified locations along the river.

edges.label: thermal energy carried by lateral inflow
edges.method: lateral discharge times lateral temperature
edges.summary: Lateral inflows add heat. Flowing and mixing water distribute that heat downstream.

edges.label: downstream water and heat export
edges.method: advective face flux with zero dispersive boundary flux
edges.summary: River flow carries water and heat out of the modeled reach.

edges.label: lumped surface heat exchange
edges.method: Newton coefficient times air-minus-water temperature
edges.summary: Water gains or loses heat according to the difference between air and water temperature. A single coefficient combines surface effects.

edges.label: shortwave, longwave, sensible, latent heat fluxes
edges.method: explicit surface budget solved by damped Newton iteration; final nonlinear flux used for accounting
edges.condition: Explicit surface budget is inactive; this scenario uses Newton exchange.
edges.summary: Sunlight, thermal radiation, evaporation, and direct heat transfer contribute separately to the surface energy balance.

edges.label: cell time-mean temperature and hydraulics
edges.method: thermal_landscape time mean, one record per cell
edges.summary: Local water temperature and flow conditions become inputs to trout habitat suitability.

edges.label: mean liquid surface-drainage increment
edges.method: illustrative mean patch runoff depth scaled to the configured catchment area and divided by the season window
edges.temporal_support: constant scalar over the configured replay
edges.condition: Requires a configured contributing catchment area; inactive in this scenario.
edges.summary: Liquid drainage from snow and soil can increase river inflow when a contributing catchment area is specified.

edges.label: benthic disturbance fraction from bed shear
edges.method: ramp from threshold to twice threshold, null maps to 0
edges.summary: Bed shear changes a modeled disturbance factor for aquatic insect development. Missing shear values receive zero disturbance in this formulation.

edges.label: chloride, arsenic and boron habitat multiplier for fish
edges.method: combined ramp from chronic to acute thresholds
edges.summary: Modeled solute concentrations modify fish suitability using authored response thresholds.

edges.label: dissolved oxygen fish habitat multiplier
edges.method: ramp between salmonid acute and growth thresholds
edges.summary: Low dissolved oxygen reduces modeled fish habitat suitability.

edges.label: dissolved oxygen insect survival factor
edges.method: ramp between insect sensitive and lethal thresholds
edges.summary: Dissolved oxygen changes the modeled survival of sensitive aquatic insect groups.

edges.label: periphyton net oxygen production and respiration
edges.units: mg O2 per m2 per s
edges.method: Platt-Jassby light response times photosynthetic quotient
edges.summary: Periphyton adds oxygen through photosynthesis and removes oxygen through respiration.

edges.label: shortwave multiplier from terrain and canopy
edges.method: sky view factor plus canopy transmissivity
edges.summary: Terrain and canopy shade reduce the sunlight reaching the river surface.

edges.label: channel to storage sensible heat exchange
edges.method: analytic two-store exchange after the implicit solve
edges.summary: Heat exchanges between channel water and a represented storage zone.

edges.label: piscivore mortality rate on trout
edges.method: sum of per-piscivore Holling II offtake with depth refuge
edges.summary: Predator density and water depth modify the modeled survival factor used in trout refuge selection.

edges.label: swallow, bat and riparian spider offtake on emergent prey
edges.method: Holling II attack and handling times per consumer
edges.summary: Emerging insects provide food for modeled swallows, bats, and riparian spiders.

edges.label: geothermal ground heat flux converted to snow melt
edges.method: heat flux divided by latent heat of fusion
edges.summary: Geothermal heat supplies energy for melting snow. The conversion uses the latent heat of fusion.

edges.label: soil temperature at root depth suppresses lodgepole
edges.method: steady conductive profile capped at local boiling point
edges.summary: A steady soil-temperature estimate reduces lodgepole suitability where the ground is too warm.

edges.label: snow depth lengthens grazer movement cost
edges.method: one plus depth over species cost half, infinite above crater depth
edges.summary: Deeper snow increases modeled movement cost and reduces grazing access.

edges.label: warm ground serves as a grazer refuge under deep snow
edges.method: warm-patch shift when snow exceeds species crater depth
edges.summary: Under deep snow, the routing model can direct grazers toward warmer ground.

edges.label: grazer dung nitrogen return to patch
edges.method: intake dry mass times 2.5 percent nitrogen fraction
edges.summary: Grazing returns nitrogen to the modeled patch stock. The conversion from intake is authored.

edges.label: grazer trampling fraction on thermal patches
edges.method: trampling fraction times authored thinning rate per step
edges.summary: Trampling reduces modeled sinter-crust thickness using an authored disturbance rate.

edges.label: reference evapotranspiration demand diagnostic
edges.method: Kc times ET0 scaled by relative soil water
edges.summary: Soil water scales a reference evapotranspiration diagnostic. The snow and soil bucket accounts for water removal.

edges.label: pool and outflow plumes raise downwind air and humidity
edges.method: bulk aerodynamic plume with internal boundary layer growth
edges.spatial_support: weather fragment downwind of the pools
edges.summary: Warm pools and outflows raise modeled downwind air temperature and humidity.

edges.label: mat state and outflow temperature set fly density
edges.method: trapezoidal temperature window times mat biomass saturation
edges.summary: Outflow temperature and microbial mat biomass set modeled food-web conditions for thermal-area flies.

edges.label: meteorological forcing
edges.summary: Air temperature, humidity, wind, and radiation supply conditions for surface heat exchange.
edges.method: Shared scenario meteorology

edges.label: snow and soil forcing
edges.summary: Air temperature and precipitation control the modeled accumulation and melting of snow and water entering the soil.
edges.method: Daily forcing for snow and soil integration

edges.label: hot outflow source
edges.summary: Authored spring temperatures and discharges supply hot water to the outflow cooling calculation.
edges.method: Prescribed spring source conditions

edges.label: outflow temperature and mat response
edges.summary: Local outflow temperature helps select the modeled microbial community and its biomass response.
edges.method: Temperature and substrate response

edges.label: canopy influence on vegetation
edges.summary: Estimated canopy coverage modifies light availability and vegetation suitability.
edges.method: Spatial canopy fraction supplied to vegetation suitability

edges.label: Dynamic flow routing
edges.summary: A momentum-based river model would represent changing discharge and water levels. The selected model prescribes inflow and uses fixed channel volumes.
edges.condition: Research extension; absent from the selected model.
edges.method: Research concept

edges.label: Winter ice cover
